facts.statement: The genus Leninia was first described by Fischer, Arkhangelsky, Uspensky, Stenshin, and Godefroit in 2013.
facts.quote: Leninia was first named by Valentin Fischer, Maxim S. Arkhangelsky, Gleb N. Uspensky, Ilya M. Stenshin and Pascal Godefroit in 2013

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was discovered in 2012 on the banks of the Volga River near the town of Kriushi inside a limestone nodule.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered in 2012, on the banks of the river Volga near the town of Kriushi in a limestone nodule.

facts.statement: Only a partial skull was found for the species Leninia.
facts.quote: Only part of the skull was found.

facts.statement: The known specimen is about 45 cm long, suggesting the total skull length was between 65 and 90 cm.
facts.quote: The specimen is around 45 cm long, which suggests the skull was between 65-90 cm long overall.

facts.statement: The maxillary dental groove in Leninia is extremely shallow, measuring only 16 mm in depth.
facts.quote: The maxillary dental groove is extremely shallow, only 16 mm deep.

facts.statement: The preserved scleral rings are made of 14 trapezoidal plates with crenulations on their inner edges.
facts.quote: Both scleral rings are preserved, but the left one is much less distorted. It is composed of 14 trapezoidal plates, with crenulations on the internal edge.

facts.statement: The scleral aperture constitutes only 11.03% of the orbital area, indicating the specimen was fully grown.
facts.quote: The scleral aperture is only 11.03% of the orbital area, suggesting that the specimen was fully grown.

facts.statement: Although the parietal bones are crushed together, there is no evidence that the skull possessed a crest.
facts.quote: The parietals are crushed against one another, but there is no evidence of a crest.

facts.statement: The name Leninia honors Vladimir Lenin indirectly, as the museum housing the fossils is located within the Lenin Memorial and Lenin school complex in Ulyanovsk.
facts.quote: It was named for Vladimir Lenin, one of the leaders of the Communist Revolution in Russia, but not directlу: the museum where fossils are housed is located within the Lenin Memorial and Lenin school complex in Ulyanovsk

facts.statement: The specific name stellans refers to the star-shaped suture between the frontal and parietal bones.
facts.quote: La segunda parte del nombre de la especie, stellans, se refiere a la sutura entre el hueso frontal y parietal, que aparece en forma de estrella en Leninia.

facts.statement: Leninia lived during the late Early Cretaceous (lower Aptian stage) in western Russia.
facts.quote: Leninia is an extinct genus of basal ophthalmosaurine ichthyosaur known from the late Early Cretaceous (lower Aptian stage) of western Russia.

facts.statement: Leninia lived between 121.4 and 119.57 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Leninia is classified as a basal ophthalmosaurine ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: Leninia is an extinct genus of basal ophthalmosaurine ichthyosaur

facts.statement: Leninia belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae and the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.
Leninia represents one of the latest-living and most basal ophthalmosaurine ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Leninia is one of the latest-living ophthalmosaurines, and also one of the most basal.

facts.statement: The large scleral ring and aperture suggest that ophthalmosaurines were specialized deep-divers with conservative ecological niches.
facts.quote: Despite this, it still had the very large scleral ring and aperture, suggesting that this was one of the most basal characteristics of ophthalmosaurines and that they were all deep-diving

facts.statement: It is debated whether the transverse crushing of the skull was caused by geological forces or the animal's death.
facts.quote: It is not known whether this was due to orogeny and rock action or to the ichthyosaur's death.

rejected.statement: The absolute size of Leninia's scleral ring is among the largest known in ichthyosaurs, exceeded only by Baptanodon and Temnodontosaurus.
rejected.quote: The absolute size of Leninia's scleral ring is among the largest known in ichthyosaurs, with only Baptanodon ('Ophthalmosaurus natans') and the giant Temnodontosaurus exceeding it.
